rubrics.evidence: “Choose independent venture building as the central learning mechanism regardless of which educational format you add.” Phases 2–5 require customer interviews, prototypes, paid pilots, an MVP and financial scenarios.
rubrics.reason: Practical venture building determines the roadmap and its decision gates. A second broad business degree is explicitly deprioritized and retained only for specific ecosystem or transition needs.

rubrics.evidence: The baseline is a “12-month validation track at 6–8 hours per week.” Phase 4 requires that a cohort’s work can be performed alongside the job, and the overload rules state: “A demanding cohort program should replace, not supplement, most self-study.”
rubrics.reason: Work and family compatibility materially constrain program selection, scheduling and workload. Intensive accelerators and degrees are conditional branches requiring explicit career and family decisions.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 1 includes applied work and interviews; Months 2–4 require 40–50 customer interviews; Months 4–6 require the “cheapest credible test,” including concierge services, deposits or small paid pilots. At Month 6: “If evidence is weak, pivot once or archive the idea.”
rubrics.reason: Discovery starts during the compact foundation period and progresses to inexpensive behavioral and payment tests before substantial program investment. Explicit kill criteria and decision gates implement staged validation.

rubrics.evidence: “Use the Business Model Canvas as a versioned hypothesis system. Update it only when evidence changes.” Phase 3 tracks payment conversion, repeat use, acquisition cost and margin potential; later phases require a 13-week cash forecast and financing scenarios.
rubrics.reason: Concrete frameworks and collected customer and market evidence drive real product, pricing, financial and continuation decisions. Although in-depth case study coverage is limited, applied, evidence-based learning clearly dominates abstract theory.

rubrics.evidence: “Avoid expensive programs dominated by general strategy, marketing or leadership content you have already covered.” The degree branch calculates tuition, living increments, lost compensation, benefits and family disruption, then compares that investment with protected venture-building time.
rubrics.reason: Cost, opportunity cost and incremental practical value materially determine route prioritization. Low-cost learning and experiments are the default, while premium programs and degrees require specific network, capability or venture-outcome advantages.
